lockFileMaintenance.description: A lockfile refresh has no reviewable content: `package.json` does not change, only transitive versions inside the ranges their parents already allow. CI passing is the whole review, so it merges itself. `platformAutomerge` is off on purpose — GitHub's own auto-merge waits for *required* status checks, and this repo has no branch protection to require any, so it would merge the moment the PR opened. With it off, Renovate waits for the checks itself before merging.

customManagers.description: actions/checkout, setup-node, etc. are `uses:` steps, so Renovate's built-in github-actions manager already tracks them by SHA. gitleaks (#551) is invoked via a plain `docker run` in a shell step instead, which no default manager scans — this picks up any `owner/image:tag@sha256:digest` reference in a workflow file, the same explicit pin shape used there.

Syft, Grype and Trivy CLI versions (#854) are passed as `with:` inputs (`syft-version`, `grype-version`, `version`) of their actions, which the built-in github-actions manager does not read. Annotate the line above the input with `# renovate: datasource=github-releases depName=owner/repo` and this picks up the value on the next line.

packageRules.description: Versions, never digests. A `uses: actions/checkout@abc123...` diff is unreviewable — you cannot tell a patch bump from a hijacked tag by reading the hash — and the same goes for a `node:26.8@sha256:...` base image. Tags are what the upgrade is judged on here, so `pinDigests` stays off even if a preset turns it on by default.

@actual-app/api and @actual-app/core are both versioned YY.M in lockstep to track the Actual server release. Bumping one ahead of the other produces out-of-sync migrations, so neither is ever automatic — both are approved by hand together when the server is upgraded.
Dev tooling: one PR for all non-major updates.
Native modules get their own PR — a rebuild failure should not be hidden inside a group.
Majors are reviewed one at a time.
